_readme.what: Indian proper nouns and loanwords -> IPA, injected as <phoneme alphabet="ipa"> into the en-US story narration by tools/tts.py. Hindi/Punjabi clips do NOT use this file: those voices are already native.
_readme.goal: The narrator keeps her English (diaspora) accent; the Indian names are said the way an Indian family says them. Not Sanskrit-pedantic, not anglicised.
engine_limits: Google's en-US phoneme set is the American English one. Symbols outside it are not an error - the API silently drops the <phoneme> tag and reads the spelling instead. Every entry here was verified against the live API on a decoy spelling, which is the only test that can tell 'honoured' from 'thrown away'. Run tools/tts.py --check-lexicon to redo it.

ASPIRATION IS RENDERABLE, and an earlier pass was wrong to say it was not. That mistake is why every Indian name in the narration was anglicised: Bhima came out 'Beema', Bharata 'Burrutuh'. Probed and accepted: bʰ ɡʰ kʰ dʒʰ tʃʰ ʈʰ ɖʰ, and the DENTAL pair d̪ʰ t̪ʰ. Do not 'simplify' d̪ʰ to dʰ or t̪ʰ to tʰ: bare dʰ and tʰ are REJECTED, and the dental diacritic U+032A is what makes the API accept them. The aspiration mark itself must be U+02B0 ʰ; the breathy-voice sign U+02B1 ʱ is rejected.
Two aspirates still have no accepted form and are written plain, with a note on the entry saying so: pʰ (so phad is pəɖ) and ɽʰ (so the -garh of Chandigarh is ɡəɽ).

Aspiration is realised as ENGLISH allophonic aspiration, so it is suppressed after a sibilant exactly as in English 'star'. Yudhishthira and Vasishtha keep their ʈʰ - the tag is honoured, the puff simply does not survive the ʂ. Nothing to fix; do not remove the mark.

PRIMARY STRESS MAY NOT FALL ON ə - probed and confirmed, ˈə is rejected outright. This is the trap that produced the old file: rather than move the stress, it changed the vowel to ʌ, the 'cup' vowel, and that single substitution is most of what made the names sound English. The rule now is the other way round - short Indian 'a' is ALWAYS ə, and the stress mark goes. Indian languages do not carry an English-shaped accent on a short a anyway, so nothing is lost.
Retroflexes ʈ ɖ ɳ ɽ ʂ are accepted and kept where they change the word. ʋ is accepted and is used for both v and w, which are one sound in most of India.
Long vowels are written with ː. Indian monophthongs are written eː / oː rather than the American diphthongs eɪ / oʊ where the difference is audible.
_readme.format: "Term": { "ipa": "...", "note": "plain-English respelling, CAPS = the syllable leaned on", "unsure": true (only where the reading is genuinely in doubt) }. The respelling is DERIVED from the ipa, not written by hand, so it cannot drift away from what the file actually asks the voice to say.
_readme.unpinned: "ipa": null with "needs_native_speaker": true means nobody here could transcribe it honestly. tools/tts.py drops those terms from the matcher entirely, so the voice reads the spelling as it would anyway. That is deliberate: a confidently wrong <phoneme> sounds authoritative and nobody ever re-checks it, whereas an obviously anglicised reading is something a parent will report. Do not fill these in by guessing - get a speaker.
_readme.matching: tools/tts.py matches case-insensitively, longest term first, on word boundaries, and handles a following possessive 's itself - do not add possessive forms here. Plural forms that actually occur in the stories are listed separately.

Krishna.note: KRISH-nuh, final -a a light schwa, not '-nuh' drawn out

Shiva.note: SHI-vuh (short i, as in 'shiver'), not SHEE-va

Siddhartha.note: si-DHAAR-thuh - both aspirates are now rendered: d̪ʰ and t̪ʰ

Shivaji.note: shi-VAA-jee (Maharashtrian speakers often stress the first syllable; VAA is the common pan-Indian reading)

Buddha.note: BU-dhuh, u as in 'put'; the dh is the dental aspirate, written d̪ʰ

Aryabhata.note: aar-yuh-bhuh-tuh - the -bhata is भट, with a retroflex ट

Singh.note: sing, no hard g at the end; सिंह is ŋ + h, not an aspirated g

Yudhishthira.note: yu-DHISH-thi-ruh - the ʈʰ is tagged but comes out unaspirated: like English, this voice drops aspiration after a sibilant

Bhima.note: BHEE-maa - the final -a is long here

syat.note: syaat - one syllable, sy- glides straight into aa

Jahanpanah.note: juh-haan-puh-NAAH ('refuge of the world', how a courtier addresses the Emperor)

kauri.note: KAW-ree - read as Hindi kaudi, the cowrie shell used as a coin

katha.note: kuh-THAA (the badge word: a story as it is told)

itihaas.note: i-ti-HAAS (the badge word: what evidence shows)

aaj.note: aaj (the badge word: how it lives today)

Thiruvananthapuram.note: ti-ru-vuh-nuhn-tuh-PU-ruhm; the Malayalam th is unaspirated here

Chandigarh.note: chuhn-dee-guhr - the -garh is ढ़, an aspirated retroflex flap; ɽʰ is rejected, so it is written ɽ

Chhattisgarh.note: chhuh-TEES-guhr - the -garh is ढ़, an aspirated retroflex flap; ɽʰ is rejected, so it is written ɽ

Panaji.note: puh-NAA-jee; Konkani speakers say Ponnji, which is further from the spelling

Imphal.note: IM-faal - the ph of इंफाल is [f], not an aspirated p

Qutub.note: KU-tub; the Arabic q is a plain k here

Gir.note: gir, short i - the forest in Gujarat

josh.note: johsh - only in 'rogan josh'; the plain English word josh is spelled the same, so this entry is deliberately about the dish

Jadoh.note: JAA-doh - Khasi dish; the Khasi vowels are only approximated here

Bhar.note: bhaar - Bengali bhand, a jester; the retroflex flap ending is approximate

Raman.note: RAA-muhn (Tenali Raman); not the physicist's RAH-mun

bhopa.note: BHOH-paa - the singer of the Pabuji phad

phad.note: puhd - the painted scroll; the ph is an aspirated p; this voice rejects pʰ outright, so it is written plain

Puri.note: PU-ree, short u - the town in Odisha

Chakli ane Kagdo.note: chuh-klee uh-NAY KAAG-doh - Gujarati for 'the sparrow and the crow'

Sngi.note: SU-ngee - Khasi Ka Sngi, the sun; English cannot begin a word with the Khasi sng- cluster, so this is an approximation

dal.note: daal, the lentils - not the English 'dal'

Dharani mandala madhyadolage.note: dhuh-ruh-NEE muhn-duh-luh muh-dhyuh-DOH-luh-gay - the opening of the Kannada song of Punyakoti; a Kannada speaker should check this one

amrita.note: uh-mri-tuh, the nectar; the t is unaspirated anyway

halahala.note: haa-luh-HAA-luh - the poison from the churning

Samudra Manthan.note: suh-MU-druh muhn-thuhn - the churning of the ocean (th plain t)

Prahlad.note: pruh-HLAAD; the fuller form Prahlada is listed separately

Bhagiratha.note: bhuh-gee-ruh-thuh (bh plain b, th plain t)

Bhagirathi.note: bhuh-gee-ruh-thee - the Ganga named after him

bhagirath prayatna.note: bhuh-gee-ruhth pruh-yuht-nuh - an enormous patient effort

Hadimba.note: huh-DIM-baa - the Kullu valley spelling of the same name

Gomaya.note: GOH-muh-yuh - the jackal and the war drum

Bhekuli Biya.note: bhay-ku-lee BI-yaa - Assamese, the frog wedding

Santhal.note: SAAN-taal - no aspirate: the autonym is Santal and the h is romanisation noise

Santhals.note: SAAN-taalz - no aspirate: the autonym is Santal and the h is romanisation noise

Thakur Jiu.note: THAA-kur JEEU - Santali, the great one

Pilchu Haram.note: PIL-choo HAA-ruhm - Santali, the first man

Pilchu Budhi.note: PIL-choo BU-dhee - Santali, the first woman

Pebet.note: PAY-bet - the Meitei tale of the small bird

Hojagiri.note: hoh-jaa-GI-ree - the Reang dance of Tripura

Bru.note: broo - what the Reang call themselves

Kwrwi.note: Kokborok spelling: the letter w stands for a vowel this transcriber cannot pin (kraw-ee? kuh-ROO-ee?). NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER - left unpinned rather than guessed.

Mailuma.note: Kokborok, the paddy goddess of the Reang. The first vowel and the stress are both guesses from the romanisation. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Mutanchi.note: Lepcha autonym, romanised inconsistently across sources. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Rongkup.note: Lepcha autonym ('children of the peak'), romanised inconsistently across sources. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Biliku.note: Great Andamanese. The spelling comes from early-twentieth-century ethnographic transcription (also written Bilik, and confused with Puluga) and cannot be read off reliably. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Abo Tani.note: AA-boh TAA-nee - the first man of the Tani peoples

Adi.note: AA-dee - one of the Tani peoples

Nyishi.note: NYEE-shee (the ny is a single sound; the engine has no palatal nasal so it is written nj)

mithun.note: MI-thun - the great half-wild cattle of the north-east

wiyus.note: Tani spirits; romanised as wiyu / uyu / ui depending on the language and the writer. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.

Kaikeyi.note: kay-KAY-yee; the ai is the vowel of 'bed', held, not the 'eye' of 'kite'

Janaki.note: jaa-nuh-KEE - Sita named as Janaka's daughter

Maithili.note: MAY-thi-lee - Sita named as the woman of Mithila

Vishvamitra.note: vi-shvaa-MI-truh - the other common romanisation of the same name

Vasishtha.note: vuh-SISH-thuh - the ʈʰ is tagged but comes out unaspirated after the sibilant

Vali.note: VAA-lee - Sugriva's brother; Bali in many tellings

Tara.note: TAA-raa - Vali's queen; the same word as the Tara of Dhruva Tara, a star

Rishyamukha.note: ri-shyuh-MOO-khuh - spelled with kh here, though the hill is often Rishyamuka with a plain k

Kanda.note: KAAN-duh - one book of the Ramayana

Kamban.note: kuhm-buhn - the Tamil poet of the Iramavataram

Anga.note: uhng-guh - the kingdom Karna is given

Uttara.note: U-tuh-raa - Virata's daughter, and the last book of the Ramayana

Brihannala.note: bri-huh-nuh-laa - Arjuna's name in the year of hiding

Ballava.note: buh-luh-vuh - Bhima's name in the year of hiding

Kanka.note: kuhng-kuh - Yudhishthira's name in the year of hiding

Sairandhri.note: say-ruhn-dhree - Draupadi's name in the year of hiding

Varanavata.note: vaa-ruh-NAA-vuh-tuh - the town with the lac house

Parva.note: puhr-vuh - one book of the Mahabharata

Lava.note: luh-vuh - Rama and Sita's son, NOT the vowel of molten lava

simsupa.note: the tree Sita sits under in the Ashoka grove. Sanskrit shimshapa / simsupa is romanised both ways and the sibilants and the second vowel are both genuinely in doubt here. NEEDS A NATIVE SPEAKER.
